title: Causal Audio-Visual Speech Enhancement with Mamba
description: An early group project exploring causal audio-visual speech enhancement with a Mamba-based architecture. The work was preliminary and was completed as part of a university group assignment.
reportTitle: Trust is All You Need: Real-Time Audio-Visual Speech Enhancement with Reliability-Aware Causal Mamba
institution: School of Electrical, Electronic, and Mechanical Engineering · University of Bristol
body:
This was group coursework, not a peer-reviewed publication. We explored real-time audio-visual speech enhancement using a causal Mamba-based system and evaluated it under noisy and disrupted visual conditions.

The report's work allocation lists my contributions to visual confidence estimation, the Scout lookahead design, the AudioNeed amplifier, the multi-task loss, fusion experiments, multi-speaker mixing, ablations, bug audits, and system integration. These were parts of a six-person project.

It was my first sustained attempt at causal audio-visual speech enhancement with recurrent state-space models. A later, single-author research project, VDBC-MAMBA-2, followed this experimentation but uses a different architecture and conditioning mechanism.
